issues.description: The problem statement/UML specifies a Stock method named addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) but the template Stock class provides addItem(StockIngredient) instead. The solution implements addToStockIngredients. This mismatch in method name/signature between the problem description and the provided template can confuse students (they may try to call addToStockIngredients as shown in the UML but the template does not compile until Stock is changed).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template consistent with the UML/problem statement by adding or renaming the method in the template Stock class to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient). For example, either rename addItem to addToStockIngredients or add a new addToStockIngredients method that delegates to the existing addItem implementation. Update any references (e.g., in Main or instructions) accordingly so students are not confused by differing method names.

issues.description: The Stock class method that adds a StockIngredient is named addItem in the template, but the problem statement UML and the solution use the name addToStockIngredients. This mismatch can confuse students when they look for the method referenced in the specification (addToStockIngredients) but only find addItem in the provided starter code.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) (and update any references) so the template, problem statement UML, and solution use the same identifier for the same concept.
